about:
How Prince is being looked at in the anchor photo: how his head and body are turned and tipped relative
to the camera (owner, 2026-11-16: "place the camera about six inches away ... exactly as it was when I
captured it, and then determine what way he is being looked at").
camera: data/cameras.json anchor_front (the depth model's camera, MoGe-2)

head.meaning: turned + = toward his own left (his nose toward the picture's right, his right cheek nearer the camera); tipped + = his left side up (a little head tilt toward his right)

body.note: from the lowest point of each peet (view-dependent points, on a soft surface): a rough reading of his body's turn

eyes_and_nostrils_only.note: the two pairs that fit best (misfit < 0.5 deg); two pairs alone leave the turn loose

summary.tipped: his left side up, about 5 deg (4-6 whatever is left out, wobbled or moved): SOLID
summary.turned: toward his own left (his nose toward the picture's right), about 5-13 deg: the DIRECTION is solid (the mirror pairs 12.7, the eye ovals 5.3, his nose right of the middle of his eyes all agree); the AMOUNT is not yet (the pairs disagree: mouth, lip corners and ear bases can be truly lopsided; pixel uncertainty alone allows roughly 0-15 deg). His measured surface (the depth model) could firm it up
summary.body: rough: about 4 deg toward his right (from his peets' lowest points)
summary.head_vs_body: his head is turned toward his left on his body and tipped; the camera was straight on and level

not_yet: his head's nod (up/down): his measured surface (the depth model) has it; not read yet
camera_tilt_note: tipped is measured against the camera's level; the owner remembers holding it straight on. His peets' line does not tip the same way, so the tip is his head, not the phone
